'''Kefeng Liu''' ({{lang-zh|s=刘克峰}}; born 12 December 1965), is a Chinese-American [[mathematician]] who is known for his contributions to [[geometric analysis]], particularly the geometry, topology and analysis of [[moduli spaces]] of [[Riemann surfaces]] and [[Calabi–Yau manifold]]s. He is a professor of mathematics at [[University of California, Los Angeles]], as well as the [[executive director]] of the [[Center of Mathematical Sciences, Zhejiang University|Center of Mathematical Sciences at Zhejiang University]]. He is best known for his collaboration with Bong Lian and [[Shing-Tung Yau]] in which they establish some [[enumerative geometry]] conjectures motivated by [[mirror symmetry]].

==Biography==
Liu was born in [[Kaifeng]], [[Henan Province|Henan province]], [[China]]. In 1985, Liu received his [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in mathematics from the Department of Mathematics of [[Peking University]] in [[Beijing]]. In 1988, Liu obtained his [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] from the Institute of Mathematics of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences|Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS)]] in Beijing.<ref name=cv/> Liu then went to study in the United States, obtaining a [[Ph.D.]] from [[Harvard University]] in 1993 under [[Shing-Tung Yau]].<ref>[http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=18836 The Mathematics Genealogy Project &ndash; Kefeng Liu]</ref>

From 1993 to 1996, Liu was [[C. L. E. Moore instructor|C. L. E. Moore Instructor]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. From 1996 to 2000, Liu was an [[assistant professor]] at [[Stanford University]]. Liu joined the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] faculty in 2000, where he was promoted to full professor in 2002.<ref name="cv">[https://www.math.ucla.edu/~liu/ Curriculum Vitae of Kefeng Liu]</ref> In September 2003, Liu was appointed as the head of [[Zhejiang University]]'s mathematics department.<ref>[http://www.zju.edu.cn/english/news/2003(1&ndash;9)/news030926b.htm Professor Kefeng Liu is Appointed as Head of Mathematical Department]</ref> Liu is currently the executive director of the Center of Mathematical Sciences at Zhejiang University.

* [[Sloan Fellowship]] (1998-2001)
* [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim Fellow]] (2002)
* Silver [[Morningside Medal]] (1998)
* [[Morningside Gold Medal in Mathematics]] (2004) 
* [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker]], 2002 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]]
